name: THE HORSES
sceneryNote: Scenery until its lines are written (reference/hitching-post/brief.md): the pointer passes through to the mud under it, so it answers no verb and names nothing. Its LOOK and LISTEN lines go in the documents first; then this goes and a hotspot is laid over it.
note: Tyler, 2026-11-07, on Main Street: "maybe we add a hitching post front and center of the camera with a few horses tied to it so that it's not just a bunch of empty space?" Then, 2026-11-08: the horses made distinct ("three copies of the same horse"), one eating, the rail at chest height, moved "quite a bit to the left"; and every one a full-sized riding horse ("they all need to look like full sized ride able horses"). A hitching rail with a black with a blaze, a palomino eating hay and a paint saddle horse, in the near mud between the letter-writer and the boundary men. Room-02 attempt 6. At dawn (Room 36) the horses are gone and the rail stands empty (Tyler, 2026-11-08: "At dawn I think the horses should all be gone. Just the hitching post is there."): a prop, art/props/room-36-hitching-rail-dawn.png. Then, 2026-11-08 (errata 197): "The three horses on main street are now a little too front and center and seem to be lit a little too bright. Can you move them back a bit, make them a bit smaller since they're moving away from the front of the screen, and make sure they're a bit dimmer for the night?" Moved from 1545,850 back into the middle ground at 1405,755 (95 px deeper, 140 px left, so Thad's stand for the false fronts at 1580,620 is not behind them); drawn by the room's depth curve there, 17% smaller, and dimmed by Main Street's figureLight.

sprite.statureNote: The rest frame, the horses' ear tips to the foot of the hay, is 1.223 of the room's man where they stand: the black's withers come to Thad's shoulder (0.82 of a man), and the other two stand as tall.
sprite.frameNote: 0 rest: the black looking out, the palomino eating, the paint over the rail · 1 the black tosses its head · 2 the palomino lifts its head from the hay · 3 the paint turns its head and swishes its tail. At rest on 0; every 7 s one of the three plays for 2.4 s, rotating (errata 77).
